title: Certify v0.2.1: d([[288,12,18]]) = 18 exactly — the first machine-checkable determination — and a first lower bound 16 <= d for [[360,12,<=24]]
description: Update to the Part B preprint (Replayable minimum-distance certificates for stabilizer codes, v0.2.0, doi:10.5281/zenodo.21799780). New certificates close the previously published interval 14 <= d <= 18 for IBM's bivariate-bicycle code [[288,12,18]] to d = 18 exactly: an explicit weight-18 logical operator (upper bound) together with LRAT unsatisfiability proofs excluding weight <= 17 (lower bound), via a translation-orbit-quotient CNF encoding, all replayable with a standard-library Python checker (qec-scripts/check_prof.py). This CONFIRMS the value asserted by Bravyi et al. (Nature 627 (2024) 778) by integer programming without a checkable artifact; it does not correct it. Also included: 16 <= d for [[360,12,<=24]] — to our knowledge the first published lower bound of any kind for that code. Independently re-verified end-to-end before release; adversarial review log in paper/FIXLOG-qec.md. Codes and asserted values are IBM's, credited; MIP methodology is Landahl-Anderson-Rice's, credited.
